newsitem.title: USA: Trading cards maker Pinnacle to join NYSE roster.
newsitem.headline: Trading cards maker Pinnacle to join NYSE roster.

text.p: Pinnacle Brands Inc hopes investors will want to trade its shares as well as its sports trading cards. The company is planning a $60 million initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange this week.

Pinnacle sells hockey, baseball and football trading cards under eight brand names including Score, Select, Pinnacle, Action Packed and Racer's Choice. In 1995, it had about a 37 percent market share in those three sports, the company said in a regulatory filing.
It plans to offer four million shares, or a one-third stake, in an offering by Merrill Lynch & Co.

Pinnacle has posted net losses since 1993. Its baseball and hockey card sales have not yet recovered from a slump suffered after the 1994 Major League Baseball strike and work stoppage at the National Hockey League.
Industry sales "have been slow to rebound and remain well below pre-strike levels," Pinnacle said in the filing.

Of the proceeds of $55 million, about $22 million will be used to reduce indebtedness under its credit agreement and $33 million would be used to repay debt from its largest shareholder, Acadia Parners LP. After the offering, Acadia will own about 65 percent of the company.
Pinnacle posted a 1995 net loss of $2.4 million on revenues of $130.2 million.
The offering is tentatively scheduled to price Wednesday for trading on Thursday.
IPO analyst Vince Slavin of Cantor Fitzgerald said the stock could rise $0.25 to $0.50 a share at its opening.
